newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen falling on political fears.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen falling on political fears.

text.p: Taiwan share prices are expected to open lower on Friday on jitters over political instability following unexpected resignations of three cabinet members ahead of a planned cabinet reshuffle, brokers said.
On Thursday, the weighted index lost 77.22 points or 0.92 percent to end at 8,349.85.

Ma Ying-jeou, minister without portfolio and a popular politician, Interior Minister Lin Feng-cheng, and Tjiu Mau-ying, chairman of Taiwan's Council of Agriculture, all tendered their resignations to premier Lien Chan on Thursday.
The administration, which has faced intense criticism over a spate of violent crime, was expected to announce a reshuffle next week.
"Increasing political uncertainty will trigger a wave of selling today," said Oliver Fang, an analyst of National Securities.

He said the market would follow the movements in parliament as lawmakers from the main opposition Democratic Progressive Party and the opposition New Party planned to seek support for a motion asking President Lee to call for a complete cabinet reshuffle and to replace Lien during Friday's session.
"Investors will turn bearish unless the government takes effective measures to boost confidence," Fang said.
Initial support was seen at 8,200 points.
